# `GLD-STD-001` v1 — Secure Coding Standard
**Kind:** standard · **Enforcement:** mandatory · **Owner:** Security Guild
_Cite as `GLD-STD-001@1` wherever you apply this._
_This item is **MANDATORY** — follow it, and state explicitly if the code or task conflicts with it._

# Secure Coding Standard

## 1. Logging
1.1 Never log secrets, passwords, API keys, tokens or full card numbers.
1.2 Log the correlation id on every request so a transaction can be traced end to end.
1.3 Log at WARN or above for anything a human must act on. INFO is for flow, not alarm.

## 2. Secrets
2.1 Secrets come from the platform's secret store, never from source, config files or environment defaults.
2.2 A secret found in source is a P1 incident, not a code-review comment.

## 3. Input validation
3.1 Validate at the boundary — controller, handler or message consumer — not deep in the domain.
3.2 Reject unknown fields rather than silently ignoring them.

## 4. Error handling
4.1 Never swallow an exception without either handling it or re-raising with context.
4.2 An error returned to a caller must not leak internal paths, SQL or stack traces.

# Dependency Health — `mini-redis` (v0.4.1)
**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Ecosystem:** Rust / Cargo
**Manifest:** `Cargo.toml` (47 lines, no `Cargo.lock` indexed)
**Standards applied:** `GLD-STD-001@1` (Secure Coding Standard — dependency/logging review)

---

## 1. Inventory

### Package metadata
| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Name | `mini-redis` | `Cargo.toml:4` |
| Version | `0.4.1` | `Cargo.toml:5` |
| Edition | 2018 | `Cargo.toml:3` |
| Binaries | `mini-redis-cli`, `mini-redis-server` | `Cargo.toml:15–21` |

### Direct dependencies (`[dependencies]`)
| Package | Declared version | File:line | Optional? | Usage evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `async-stream` | `0.3.0` (exact minor) | `Cargo.toml:24` | No | `src/cmd/subscribe.rs:179`, `src/clients/client.rs:8` |
| `atoi` | `2.0.0` (exact minor) | `Cargo.toml:25` | No | `src/frame.rs:251`, `src/parse.rs:101` |
| `bytes` | `1` (major wildcard) | `Cargo.toml:26` | No | 12 call sites across `src/` |
| `clap` | `4.2.7` (exact minor), feature `derive` | `Cargo.toml:27` | No | CLI argument parsing |
| `tokio` | `1` (major wildcard), feature `full` | `Cargo.toml:28` | No | Async runtime — used pervasively |
| `tokio-stream` | `0.1` (major wildcard) | `Cargo.toml:29` | No | Async stream utilities |
| `tracing` | `0.1.34` (exact minor) | `Cargo.toml:30` | No | 7 call sites across `src/` |
| `tracing-subscriber` | `0.3.11` (exact minor), feature `env-filter` | `Cargo.toml:31` | No | Subscriber/logging setup |
| `opentelemetry` | `0.20.0` | `Cargo.toml:33` | Yes (`otel`) | OTel spec types |
| `tracing-opentelemetry` | `0.21.0` | `Cargo.toml:35` | Yes (`otel`) | tracing ↔ OTel bridge |
| `opentelemetry-aws` | `0.8.0` | `Cargo.toml:37` | Yes (`otel`) | X-Ray propagator |
| `opentelemetry-otlp` | `0.13.0` | `Cargo.toml:39` | Yes (`otel`) | OTel OTLP exporter |

### Dev dependencies (`[dev-dependencies]`)
| Package | Declared version | File:line | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokio` | `1`, feature `test-util` | `Cargo.toml:43` | Duplicate of runtime dep; scoped to tests only — correct pattern |

### Feature flags
| Feature | Gates | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `otel` | `opentelemetry`, `tracing-opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry-aws`, `opentelemetry-otlp` | `Cargo.toml:46` |

> **Note:** `Cargo.lock` was **not found** in the indexed repository. This means resolved
> (transitive) versions cannot be inspected here. All findings below are based solely on the
> declared `Cargo.toml` constraints.

---

## 2. Version Drift & Duplicates

### `tokio` pinned at two different feature sets
**Observed.** `tokio` appears twice with the same semver range (`"1"`) but different feature sets:

| Location | Version | Features |
|---|---|---|
| `Cargo.toml:28` | `"1"` | `full` |
| `Cargo.toml:43` | `"1"` | `test-util` |

This is **not a conflict** — Cargo merges feature sets per profile. However, `features = ["full"]`
enables every Tokio feature (including `io-std`, `net`, `rt-multi-thread`, `time`, `signal`, etc.),
which inflates compile time and binary size. This is a known trade-off for tutorial/example projects
but would be worth tightening for a production build.

### No other drift detected
All other packages appear exactly once. No conflicting pinned versions were found across modules
(single-crate repo).

---

## 3. Upgrade Candidates

The concerns below are based on **known release cadence and age of the pinned versions** as of
2026-07-26. Actual latest versions and any CVEs must be confirmed with `cargo outdated` /
`cargo audit` (see §4).

| Package | Current Pin | Concern | Priority | How to Confirm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opentelemetry` | `0.20.0` | **Unverified** — OTel Rust crates have had frequent breaking releases (0.21, 0.22, 0.23, 0.24+). v0.20 is likely several majors behind; API surface is large and ecosystem drift is high. | 🔴 High candidate | `cargo outdated -p opentelemetry` |
| `opentelemetry-otlp` | `0.13.0` | **Unverified** — Moves in lockstep with `opentelemetry`; 0.13 paired with 0.20 core. Multiple newer releases likely exist. | 🔴 High candidate | `cargo outdated -p opentelemetry-otlp` |
| `tracing-opentelemetry` | `0.21.0` | **Unverified** — Bridges `tracing` 0.1 and `opentelemetry`; version must stay in sync with both. 0.21 is likely stale relative to current OTel core. | 🔴 High candidate | `cargo outdated -p tracing-opentelemetry` |
| `opentelemetry-aws` | `0.8.0` | **Unverified** — Tracks OTel core; likely stale. Small ecosystem impact but must move with the others if the `otel` feature is used. | 🟠 Medium candidate | `cargo outdated -p opentelemetry-aws` |
| `clap` | `4.2.7` | **Unverified** — clap 4.x has been actively maintained; 4.2.7 (released ~2023) may be several patch/minor versions behind current 4.x. No known security history for clap itself. | 🟡 Low–Medium | `cargo outdated -p clap` |
| `tracing` | `0.1.34` | **Unverified** — `tracing` 0.1.x is stable and mature; 0.1.34 may be a few patches behind but the API is stable. Low urgency. | 🟡 Low | `cargo outdated -p tracing` |
| `tracing-subscriber` | `0.3.11` | **Unverified** — Same family as `tracing`; minor patches may exist. | 🟡 Low | `cargo outdated -p tracing-subscriber` |
| `async-stream` | `0.3.0` (exact minor) | **Unverified** — Pinned to exact minor `0.3.0` (no patch flexibility). Patches may contain bug fixes. Consider loosening to `"0.3"`. | 🟡 Low | `cargo outdated -p async-stream` |
| `atoi` | `2.0.0` (exact minor) | **Unverified** — Pinned to exact minor. Same concern as `async-stream`. Stable, small crate but patches would not be received. | 🟢 Low | `cargo outdated -p atoi` |
| `bytes` | `1` (wildcard) | **Unverified** — Wide pin is fine for flexibility; `bytes 1.x` is stable. Verify no known issues. | 🟢 Informational | `cargo outdated -p bytes` |
| `tokio` | `1` (wildcard) | **Unverified** — Wide pin is fine; Tokio 1.x is actively maintained. `features = ["full"]` may be worth narrowing. | 🟢 Informational | `cargo outdated -p tokio` |

#### Rust Edition note
**Observed:** `edition = "2018"` (`Cargo.toml:3`). Rust 2021 edition is current stable and brings
resolver v2 (better feature deduplication), improved closure captures, and other ergonomic fixes.
Migrating is low-risk (`cargo fix --edition`) and worth doing, especially for a codebase used as a
learning reference.

---

## 4. Security Surface Notes (GLD-STD-001@1)

Reviewing against the Secure Coding Standard mandatory rules:

| Rule | Finding |
|---|---|
| **2.1 – Secrets from secret store** | No secrets were found embedded in `Cargo.toml`. The OTel/OTLP exporter (`opentelemetry-otlp`) will need endpoint configuration at runtime; verify no API keys or tokens are hard-coded in source. **Action:** run `cargo audit` to check for known CVEs in deps that handle network I/O. |
| **1.1 – Never log secrets** | `tracing` is used for structured logging at 7 call sites. **Unverified** whether any log statements emit sensitive data; a code-level review of those sites is recommended. |
| **4.2 – Errors must not leak internals** | `bytes`, `tokio`, and `clap` all surface error types; confirm error handling at the server boundary (`src/server.rs`) does not relay internal detail to clients. |

No P1 secret-in-source findings were detected in `Cargo.toml`.

---

## 5. Verification Commands

Run all of the following to turn every "Unverified" candidate above into a confirmed (or cleared)
finding:

```bash
# 1. Install the tools (one-time)
cargo install cargo-audit
cargo install cargo-outdated

# 2. Check for known CVEs in the dependency tree (direct + transitive)
#    Requires Cargo.lock to be present; generate first if absent:
cargo generate-lockfile
cargo audit

# 3. Show all outdated direct dependencies and their available upgrades
cargo outdated --depth 1

# 4. Show ALL outdated packages (including transitive) — use to spot hidden issues
cargo outdated

# 5. Per-package targeted checks (e.g. the high-priority OTel cluster)
cargo outdated -p opentelemetry
cargo outdated -p opentelemetry-otlp
cargo outdated -p tracing-opentelemetry
cargo outdated -p opentelemetry-aws

# 6. Migrate Rust edition (dry run first)
cargo fix --edition --dry-run
# Then apply:
cargo fix --edition

# 7. After any upgrades, re-run the full test suite
cargo test --all-features
```

> **Note:** `cargo audit` requires a `Cargo.lock` file. If this repo does not commit one
> (common for libraries), generate it locally with `cargo generate-lockfile` before auditing.
> Application binaries should commit `Cargo.lock` so the resolved tree is reproducible and
> auditable in CI.

---

## 6. Summary & Prioritised Actions

| Priority | Action |
|---|---|
| 🔴 1 | **Generate `Cargo.lock` and run `cargo audit`** — no security advisory baseline exists without it. |
| 🔴 2 | **Upgrade the OTel cluster** (`opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `tracing-opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry-aws`) together — they must version-match and are likely several majors behind. |
| 🟠 3 | **Commit `Cargo.lock`** to source control — this is a binary crate; not committing the lockfile makes builds non-reproducible and CI audits impossible. |
| 🟡 4 | **Update `clap`**, `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber` to latest 4.x / 0.1.x / 0.3.x respectively. |
| 🟡 5 | **Loosen `async-stream` and `atoi` pins** from `"0.3.0"` / `"2.0.0"` to `"0.3"` / `"2"` so patch releases are automatically received. |
| 🟢 6 | **Migrate to Rust edition 2021** via `cargo fix --edition`. |
| 🟢 7 | **Narrow `tokio` features** from `"full"` to only those actually used (reduces compile time and binary size). |

---
*All version concerns are marked **Unverified** — confirmed findings require `cargo outdated` and
`cargo audit` output. Report produced by Dependency Health Agent on 2026-07-26.*
